title: Brampton residents shocked &amp#039;good&amp#039; neighbour opened fire in courthouse as SIU searches for motive
subtitle: A neighbour of a man shot dead by Peel Police on Friday after he apparently opened fire in a courthouse describes Charnjit 'Sonny' Singh Bassi as 'a good man'
article: A neighbour of a man shot dead by Peel Regional Police on Friday after he apparently opened fire in the Brampton courthouse describes Charnjit Singh Bassi as "a good man."
"I don't see anything wrong with that man," said Nadia Gewarges, a mother of three who has lived for 10 years on Flower Trail Road, a few houses down from Mr. Bassi.

Her comments come three days after the courthouse on Main Street in Brampton erupted in pandemonium Friday when a man opened fire inside the courthouse entrance, wounding Const. Michael Klarenbeek, a court security officer. Police later shot the man dead. Authorities then locked down the busy courthouse for most of the day.
The provincial agency charged with investigating shootings involving police, the Special Investigations Unit, said Monday that the man shot by police is Charnjit Bassi, 45, of Brampton.
Peel Regional Police released a photograph of Mr. Bassi, adding that he went by his nickname, "Sonny."
It remains unclear whether he was at the courthouse for legal reasons.
Neighbours said Mr. Bassi lived many years on quiet Flower Trail Road in Brampton. He had apparently separated from his wife, with whom he had a daughter, who is now seven.

Mrs. Gewarges says that Mr. Bassi's ex-wife also lives on Flower Trail Road, about 10 houses away from her ex-husband. The woman was not friendly and did not respond when she said hi, she said. Mr. Bassi, however, always responded politely.
Mrs. Gewarges said that her husband Zaya Gewarges, an auto mechanic, fixed Mr. Bassi's car as well as a car belonging to Mr. Bassi's sister.
"Sonny came, he fixed his car, there was no problem," she said. "Sonny paid my husband."
The woman, who immigrated from Iraq, said that her neighbours, of Italian and South Asian background, all get along well.

She said that her children, aged 10, eight and seven, often played in front of Mr. Bassi's house because it opens into a turnaround in that section. But on the weekend the children did not play there. Peel police vehicles were parked there, while officers searched Mr. Bassi's house.

Const. George Tudos, a spokesman for Peel police, said Monday that Cont. Klarenbeek is on the mend at Sunnybrook hospital in north Toronto. "He is recovering. He is with family," Const. Tudos said. "He has been taken out of the ICU. He is in good spirits, and overwhelmed with all the support that he has been receiving."
Const. Tudos said he has taken use of force classes taught by Const. Klarenbeek, a 29-year veteran of the force.
"He's very friendly and approachable," Const. Tudos said.
In a news release, the SIU said that it, "continues to have 15 investigators and three forensic investigators probing the circumstances of this incident."

Peel homicide investigators, "are conducting a full investigation into the actions and activities of the deceased leading up to the events that transpired that morning," police said in a release. "In particular, investigators are trying to determine what brought Mr. Bassi to the Brampton Courthouse and his intentions on that date."
The courthouse was open for business on Monday, with a stronger police presence than normal.
